<reason>CON won because the motion required rates, ethics, and distress together, and A made that joint burden decisive. Spain/Wales plus the admission that a clean default-only test “almost never exists” left the rate claim confounded; the vise then showed any extra yeses come from scoring family ignorance as retrieval rather than refusal. PRO stayed coherent on complementarity and listed-patient harm, but never escaped that the gain and the alleged non-violation were the same cases.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's vise, crystallized in R2 and the closing daughter scene: if the default changes no answers, rates fail; if it converts hesitation into a yes, ethics fail on the same organs.</best_rebuttal>
